'''Steven T. Bramwell''' (born 7 June 1961) is a British [[physicist]] and [[chemist]] who works at the [[London Centre for Nanotechnology]] and the Department of Physics and Astronomy,  [[University College London]]. He is known for his experimental discovery of [[spin ice]] with M. J. Harris and his calculation of a [[critical exponent]] observed in two-dimensional magnets with P. C. W. Holdsworth. A probability distribution for global quantities in complex systems,
the "Bramwell-Holdsworth-Pinton (BHP) distribution", (to be implemented in [[Mathematica]]<ref>{{cite web|last=Trott|first=Michael; Marichev, Oleg|title=The Ultimate Univariate Probability Distribution Explorer|url=http://blog.wolfram.com/2013/02/01/the-ultimate-univariate-probability-distribution-explorer/|publisher=blog.wolfram.com|access-date=March 23, 2013|date=February 1, 2013}}</ref>) is named after him.<ref>{{cite web |last=Crooks |first=Gavin E. |title=Survey of simple, continuous, univariate probability distributions |website=Three Plus One |s2cid=18883018 |url=http://threeplusone.com/gec/media/Crooks-GUDv5.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706060322/http://threeplusone.com/gec/media/Crooks-GUDv5.pdf |archive-date=2017-07-06}}</ref>

Bramwell studied chemistry at [[Oxford University]], obtaining his [[PhD]] in 1989. He was a professor of [[physical chemistry]] at [[University College London]] from 2000-2009, before becoming a Professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy.

==Honours and distinctions==
Bramwell was awarded the 2010 [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize|Holweck Prize]] of the British [[Institute of Physics]] and the Société Française de Physique (SFP) for "pioneering new concepts in the experimental and theoretical study of spin systems".<ref name=holweck>{{cite web|title=2010 Holweck medal and prize|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/bilateral/holweck/medallists/page_44442.html|publisher=iop.org|access-date=March 23, 2013}}</ref>  He shared the 2012 [[Europhysics Prize]] of the [[European Physical Society]] Condensed Matter Division "for the prediction and experimental observation of magnetic monopoles in spin ice".<ref name=europhysics>{{cite web|title=EPS CMD Europhysics Prize|url=http://www.epsnews.eu/2012/06/2012-eps-cmd-europhysics-prize/|publisher=epsnews.eu|access-date=March 23, 2013|date=June 28, 2012}}</ref>  He is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].

In 2010 he won the [[Times Higher Education]] research project of the year for "magnetricity",<ref>{{cite web|title=EPSRC researchers win 'Research project of the year' at the Times Higher Education Awards|url=http://www.epsrc.ac.uk/newsevents/news/2010/Pages/theawards.aspx|publisher=epsrc.ac.uk|access-date=March 23, 2013|date=November 30, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120715005332/http://www.epsrc.ac.uk/newsevents/news/2010/Pages/theawards.aspx|archive-date=July 15, 2012}}</ref>  and was named by [[The Times]] on their list of the 100 top [[United Kingdom|UK]] scientists.<ref>{{cite web|last=Durrani|first=Matin|title=100 top UK scientists revealed|url=http://blog.physicsworld.com/2010/10/07/100-top-uk-scientists-revealed/|publisher=blog.physicsworld.com|access-date=March 23, 2013|date=Oct 7, 2010}}</ref>

In 2019, Bramwell was awarded an honorary doctorate (FDhc) at [[Uppsala University]] in recognition of his work on spin ice, two-dimensional magnetism and longstanding collaboration with researchers at the [[Ångström Laboratory]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-10-31 |title=New honorary doctors at Uppsala University - Uppsala University |url=https://www.uu.se/en/news/2018/2018-10-31-new-honorary-doctors-at-uppsala-university |access-date=2025-05-18 |website=www.uu.se |language=en}}</ref>
